subject: management-of-business
title: Inventory Control: The Sawtooth Stock Chart

slides.heading: Inventory Control: The Sawtooth Stock Chart
bullets: How one stocked item is controlled on the sawtooth stock chart: stock starts at the maximum level of 1,000 units, falls at a steady usage rate of 125 units a day, crosses the reorder level of 500 units to fire a new order, falls through the 2-day lead time to the buffer stock of 250 units, and jumps back to maximum when the delivery lands
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we read the sawtooth stock chart level by level and watch exactly when an order must be placed.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Read the three governing levels on the chart: maximum stock level 1,000 units, reorder level 500 units and buffer stock 250 units
Explain why the order fires when stock falls to the reorder level on day 4, and why stock bottoms out at the buffer of 250 units on day 6 as the delivery lands
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to predict the next order day from the chart alone.

slides.heading: Stock is still half full - so why order now?
bullets: The chart shows 500 units still in stock, yet that is exactly the moment the new order must be placed
If ordering can wait, why not wait until the shelves are actually empty?
slides.notes: Ask the class: would you order while half the stock remains? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the lead time is the missing piece.

slides.heading: The reorder level already accounts for the lead time
bullets: Deliveries take a lead time to arrive, and stock keeps falling while the order is on its way
The reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage: 250 + (2 x 125) = 500 units
Buffer stock is the safety floor stock should never fall below, not spare stock to be used up first
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: reorder level = buffer stock + lead-time usage, so ordering at 500 units leaves exactly enough stock to survive the lead time.

slides.heading: Three levels govern the chart: maximum, reorder, buffer
bullets: Stock starts full at the maximum stock level of 1,000 units
The reorder level of 500 units is the trigger line, and the buffer stock of 250 units is the safety floor below it
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the three lines in order: maximum at the top, reorder in the middle, buffer near the bottom.

slides.heading: Stock falls steadily - crossing the reorder level fires the order
bullets: Steady usage of 125 units a day pulls stock down in a straight slope from 1,000 units
The moment the falling line crosses the reorder level of 500 units on day 4, a new order is placed
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and stop at the crossing point: the order fires on day 4, while 500 units remain - not when stock runs out.

slides.heading: Through the lead time to the buffer - then the delivery jumps stock back up
bullets: Through the 2-day lead time stock keeps falling, from 500 units down to the buffer stock of 250 units
On day 6 the delivery lands and the stock line jumps straight back up to the maximum level of 1,000 units
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and point to the lowest point: stock touches the buffer exactly as the delivery arrives, and never falls below it.

slides.heading: The sawtooth repeats: fall, reorder, wait, delivery, jump
bullets: Nothing has changed, so the cycle repeats: stock falls again at the same steady rate
Falling stock crosses the reorder level again on day 10 to fire the next order, giving the repeating sawtooth shape
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and trace the second tooth with your finger: fall, reorder, wait, delivery, jump - the same five beats.

slides.heading: Worked example: reading one full cycle
bullets: Usage is 125 units a day, so stock falls from 1,000 to the reorder level of 500 in 4 days, and lead-time usage is 2 x 125 = 250 units
Reorder level = buffer 250 + lead-time usage 250 = 500 units, and stock bottoms at 250 units on day 6 as the delivery lands
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, find the usage rate - 125 units a day. Step 2, time the fall to the reorder level - 4 days. Step 3, value the lead-time usage - 250 units. Step 4, check the floor - stock bottoms at the buffer of 250 units on day 6.

slides.heading: Your turn: when does the next order fire?
bullets: In pairs: starting full at 1,000 units on day 6 with usage still 125 units a day, state the day stock reaches the reorder level and the day the next delivery lands
Then swap and check: did your partner use the reorder level of 500 units, not zero, as the trigger?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the full chain, then take two pairs answers: reorder on day 10, delivery on day 12, stock bottoming at the buffer of 250 units.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who would wait until stock runs out before ordering
Name the reorder level, the lead time and the buffer stock to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers show stock bottoming out at the buffer just as the delivery lands.
